content.comment_body: I'm new to [product_name] and have not been able to find a solution to my issue in the [product_name] forum. I suspect it's a straightforward problem, likely due to my lack of experience with [product_name]. After creating and downloading the attached [product_name] program and [product_name] [version_no], as well as transferring it to my [product_name] [version_no], I noticed the push button does not remain green after activation and instead shows a rotating timer icon. I'm unsure how to resolve this. I want the button to stay green when activated and turn red when deactivated, without the rotating icon. Can someone help me understand what I'm missing? Thank you.

I'm not sure why you've created a new topic. As mentioned previously: what you're attempting is not possible. The variable [article_no] is assigned to the push button, which is set up to respond to mouse clicks and therefore only generates a brief pulse. [article_no] remains active only as long as the pulse lasts, so the push button is green only momentarily. If you want a display to stay green for the entire duration, you'll need to design your own visualization using Q1. Instead of showing the hourglass, select green as the color in your custom display.

analysis.insight_summary: A user experienced confusion with the push button function in [product_name]: when activated, it quickly turns green and shows a timer icon rather than staying green, which was expected. The user attributes the issue to limited experience. Another participant explained the push button's default behavior provides only a short pulse, clarifying the situation and highlighting the difference between user expectation and actual UI feedback.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the push button to remain green while active and to turn red when deactivated, omitting the timer icon and visually reflecting the persistent on/off status.
